lesson.title: Words for chance
lesson.body: Impossible, unlikely, as likely as not, likely, certain. A probability puts a number on it: 0 is impossible, 1 is certain, and 1/2 is as likely as not.

lesson.title: Not happening
lesson.body: The probability that something does not happen is 1 minus the probability that it does: if rain is 3/10, no rain is 7/10.

lesson.title: Wanted out of all
lesson.body: List every equally likely outcome. The probability is the number you want out of all of them: an even number on a die is 3 out of 6 = 1/2.

lesson.title: Count things, not kinds
lesson.body: A bag with 1 red and 9 blue marbles has two colours, but red is 1 out of 10, not 1 out of 2.

lesson.title: List carefully
lesson.body: Two coins can land HH, HT, TH or TT: four outcomes. HT and TH are different, so one head and one tail is 2 out of 4.

lesson.title: Expecting
lesson.body: If red has probability 1/4, in 40 spins you would expect about 1/4 × 40 = 10 reds: about, not exactly.

templates.construct: Find the probability that an event does not happen

formats.prompt: The probability that it rains tomorrow is {frac(p)}. What is the probability that it does not rain?
The probability that a team wins its next game is {frac(p)}. There are no draws. What is the probability that it does not win?

hints: It either happens or it does not: the two probabilities add up to 1.

distractors.feedback: {frac(value)} is the probability that it does happen. The two add up to 1.

templates.construct: Give a probability as a per cent

formats.prompt: A box has {total} raffle tickets, and {w} of them win a prize. What is the probability of picking a winning ticket, as a per cent?

hints: Probability = winning tickets ÷ all tickets.
{w} out of {total} = {w}/{total}.
Make it out of 100: × {100 / total}.

distractors.feedback: {value}% is the number of winning tickets. Write {w} out of {total} as a per cent.
{value}% is the chance of not winning. The question asks about winning.

templates.construct: Find a probability on one die by listing the outcomes

formats.prompt: A fair die is rolled. What is the probability of rolling {(ev == 1 ? 'a 5' : (ev == 2 ? 'an even number' : (ev == 3 ? 'a number greater than 4' : (ev == 4 ? 'a multiple of 3' : (ev == 5 ? 'a prime number' : 'a number less than 3')))))}?

hints: A die has 6 equally likely outcomes: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6.
The outcomes you want are {(ev == 1 ? '5' : (ev == 2 ? '2, 4 and 6' : (ev == 3 ? '5 and 6' : (ev == 4 ? '3 and 6' : (ev == 5 ? '2, 3 and 5' : '1 and 2')))))}.
{n} out of 6: simplify the fraction.

distractors.feedback: {frac(value)} compares the outcomes you want with the others. Probability compares them with all 6.
{frac(value)} counts one outcome too many. The ones you want are {(ev == 1 ? '5' : (ev == 2 ? '2, 4 and 6' : (ev == 3 ? '5 and 6' : (ev == 4 ? '3 and 6' : (ev == 5 ? '2, 3 and 5' : '1 and 2')))))}.

templates.construct: Find the probability of picking a colour from a bag

formats.prompt: A bag has {r} red, {g} green and {bl} blue marbles. You pick one without looking. What is the probability that it is {colour}?

hints: Probability = the {colour} marbles ÷ all the marbles.
There are {n} {colour} marbles and {total} in all.
{n}/{total}: simplify it.

distractors.feedback: {frac(value)} treats the three colours as equally likely. Count the marbles: {n} of {total}.
{frac(value)} compares {colour} with the other marbles. Probability is out of all {total}.

templates.construct: Find a probability on a numbered spinner

formats.prompt: A spinner has {sides} equal parts numbered 1 to {sides}. What is the probability that it lands on a number less than {k}?

hints: List the numbers less than {k}.
They are 1 to {k - 1}: {k - 1} of them.
{k - 1} out of {sides}: simplify it.
templates.explain: {k - 1} of the {sides} numbers are less than {k}: {frac(answer)}.

distractors.feedback: {frac(value)} counts {k} too. Less than {k} means 1 to {k - 1}.
{frac(value)} compares with the other numbers. Probability is out of all {sides}.

templates.construct: Find the probability of picking a multiple from numbered cards

formats.prompt: Cards numbered 1 to {cn} are shuffled. You pick one. What is the probability that it is a multiple of {m}?

hints: Count the multiples of {m} from 1 to {cn}.
The last multiple of {m} up to {cn} is {n * m} = {n} × {m}, so there are {n} of them.
{n} out of {cn}: simplify it.
templates.explain: {n} of the {cn} cards are multiples of {m}: {frac(answer)}.

distractors.feedback: {frac(value)} is 1 in {m}. Count the multiples of {m} up to {cn}: {n} of {cn}.
{frac(value)} counts one card too many. The multiples of {m} up to {cn} are {n}.

templates.construct: Find a probability with two or three coins by listing the outcomes

formats.prompt: {ev <= 3 ? 'Two coins are' : 'Three coins are'} tossed. What is the probability of getting {(ev == 1 ? 'two heads' : (ev == 2 ? 'one head and one tail' : (ev == 3 ? 'at least one head' : (ev == 4 ? 'three heads' : 'exactly two heads'))))}?

hints: List every way the coins can land, H for heads and T for tails.
They are {ev <= 3 ? 'HH, HT, TH and TT' : 'HHH, HHT, HTH, HTT, THH, THT, TTH and TTT'}.
The ones you want are {(ev == 1 ? 'HH' : (ev == 2 ? 'HT and TH' : (ev == 3 ? 'HH, HT and TH' : (ev == 4 ? 'HHH' : 'HHT, HTH and THH'))))}.
steps: All outcomes: {ev <= 3 ? 'HH, HT, TH and TT' : 'HHH, HHT, HTH, HTT, THH, THT, TTH and TTT'}
Wanted: {(ev == 1 ? 'HH' : (ev == 2 ? 'HT and TH' : (ev == 3 ? 'HH, HT and TH' : (ev == 4 ? 'HHH' : 'HHT, HTH and THH'))))}
templates.explain: {(ev == 1 ? 'HH' : (ev == 2 ? 'HT and TH' : (ev == 3 ? 'HH, HT and TH' : (ev == 4 ? 'HHH' : 'HHT, HTH and THH'))))} out of {ev <= 3 ? 'HH, HT, TH and TT' : 'HHH, HHT, HTH, HTT, THH, THT, TTH and TTT'}: {frac(answer)}.

distractors.feedback: {frac(value)} misses some outcomes. HT and TH are different; list all {ev <= 3 ? 'four' : 'eight'}: {ev <= 3 ? 'HH, HT, TH and TT' : 'HHH, HHT, HTH, HTT, THH, THT, TTH and TTT'}.

templates.construct: Find the probability of a total with two dice

formats.prompt: Two fair dice are rolled and the numbers are added. What is the probability that the total is {s}?

hints: Two dice have 6 × 6 = 36 equally likely outcomes.
{w} out of 36: simplify it.

distractors.feedback: {frac(value)} treats the 11 totals, 2 to 12, as equally likely. Count the 36 pairs: {w} of them total {s}.
{frac(value)} is out of 6. Two dice have 6 × 6 = 36 outcomes.

templates.construct: Find how many times to expect an outcome

formats.prompt: A spinner has {parts} equal parts, and {red} of them are red. It is spun {t} times. About how many times would you expect it to land on red?

hints: The probability of red is {red}/{parts}.
Expect about {red}/{parts} of the {t} spins.
{t} ÷ {parts} × {red} = ?

distractors.feedback: {value} is the spins expected not to land on red. The question asks about red.
{value} is {t} × {red}. Take {red}/{parts} of {t}: divide by {parts} too.

templates.construct: Compare the chance of red in two bags of different sizes

answer.label: {pick(value, 'Bag A', 'Bag B', 'Both the same', 'You cannot tell')}

formats.prompt: Bag A has {aR} red marble{aR == 1 ? '' : 's'} out of {aN}. Bag B has {bR} red marble{bR == 1 ? '' : 's'} out of {bN}. You pick one marble from one bag without looking. Which bag gives a better chance of red?

hints: The chance of red is the red marbles out of all the marbles in that bag.
Bag A: {aR}/{aN}. Bag B: {bR}/{bN}.
It is not 'You cannot tell': write both chances with the same bottom number and compare.
steps: {best == 1 ? 'Bag A' : 'Bag B'} gives the better chance
templates.explain: With the same bottom number, {aN * bN}, Bag A gives {aR * bN} and Bag B gives {bR * aN}. {best == 1 ? 'Bag A' : 'Bag B'} is better, even though {best == 1 ? 'Bag B' : 'Bag A'} has more red marbles.

distractors.feedback: {pick(value, 'Bag A', 'Bag B', 'Both the same', 'You cannot tell')} has more red marbles, but also more marbles in all. Compare the chances, {aR}/{aN} and {bR}/{bN}, not the counts.
The chances are {aR}/{aN} and {bR}/{bN}, which are not equal. Write them with the same bottom number to see which is bigger.
You can tell: the chance in each bag is its red marbles out of all its marbles, {aR}/{aN} and {bR}/{bN}. Compare them.

templates.construct: Work back from a probability and a count to the number of outcomes

formats.prompt: A bag holds red and blue marbles. The probability of picking red is {num}/{den}. There are {r} red marbles. How many marbles are in the bag?

hints: A probability of {num}/{den} means {num} out of every {den} marbles {num == 1 ? 'is' : 'are'} red.
{r} ÷ {num} = {k}, so there are {k} groups of {den} marbles, each with {num} red.
templates.explain: {r} red marbles are {num}/{den} of the bag, so it holds {r} ÷ {num} × {den} = {answer} marbles.

distractors.feedback: {value} is the blue marbles. The question asks for all the marbles, red and blue together.
{value} is {r} × {den}. Only {num} in every {den} are red: divide {r} by {num} first.

templates.construct: Find a probability for a spinner and a coin together, by counting outcomes

formats.prompt: A spinner has {p} equal parts numbered 1 to {p}. You spin it and toss a coin. What is the probability of {pick(ev, 'an even number', 'an odd number', 'a number greater than 2', 'a 1')} and {side == 1 ? 'heads' : 'tails'}?

hints: Each of the {p} numbers can come with heads or with tails: {2 * p} outcomes in all.
{f} of the {p} numbers {f == 1 ? 'is' : 'are'} {pick(ev, 'even', 'odd', 'greater than 2', 'equal to 1')}, and each comes with {side == 1 ? 'heads' : 'tails'} once.
{f} out of {2 * p} = ?
templates.explain: {f} of the {2 * p} equally likely outcomes fit, so the probability is {frac(answer)}.

distractors.feedback: {frac(value)} leaves out the coin. Each number comes with heads or tails, so there are {2 * p} outcomes.
1/2 is the coin alone. The spinner must land on {pick(ev, 'an even number', 'an odd number', 'a number greater than 2', 'a 1')} too.
{frac(value)} adds the {p} numbers and the 2 sides. Multiply them: {2 * p} outcomes.

templates.construct: Tell an impossible or a certain event from the faces of a die

answer.label: {pick(value, 'Rolling a 7', 'Rolling a number less than 7', 'Rolling an even number', 'Rolling a 6')}

formats.prompt: A fair die with faces 1 to 6 is rolled. Which of these is {q == 1 ? 'impossible' : 'certain'}?

hints: A die shows 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 or 6.
Impossible means it can never happen; certain means it happens every time.
{q == 1 ? 'Which one can never happen?' : 'Which one happens on every roll?'}
steps: {q == 1 ? 'No face shows 7' : 'Every face is less than 7'}
So {pick(q, 'rolling a 7 is impossible', 'rolling a number less than 7 is certain')}
templates.explain: {pick(q, 'No face shows 7, so rolling a 7 is impossible.', 'Every face, 1 to 6, is less than 7, so rolling a number less than 7 is certain.')}
